note.question: Can a platform profitably communicate demand information to competing sellers by reporting a region rather than a point forecast, even though its message is nonbinding and its commission rises with seller revenue?
note.overview: This is an incomplete-information cheap-talk game between an informed platform and strategically pricing sellers.

models.method: To achieve this goal, we develop a stylized model in which a group of sellers, who compete by setting prices, use an e-commerce platform to sell their products.

sources.quote: In stage 1, the platform observes the value of θ; in stage 2, the platform shares a message m with the sell­ ers, and based on the shared information, each seller forms a posterior belief about the potential market demand, captured by f(θ|m); in stage 3, all sellers deter­ mine their prices simultaneously; finally, in stage 4, the platform and each of the sellers observe their respective payoffs.

components.label: Region-forecast information-sharing equilibrium
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Region-forecast information-sharing equilibrium (partition cheap-talk equilibrium); no meaningful point-forecast equilibrium when products are substitutes. The paper constructs posterior-consistent interval messages and seller price best responses, and selects the sender-preferred/Pareto-dominant maximum-interval partition.
